Sapphire
SAF-eye-er
noun
Greek sappheiros (G4552), Hebrew sappir (H5601) — a deep blue precious stone; the second foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:19) and the very stone underfoot when the elders of Israel beheld God on Sinai: "under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone" (Exod 24:10). The biblical sapphire was likely lapis lazuli — opaque deep blue with golden flecks — though the corundum gem we now call sapphire also matches the color.

📖 Biblical Definition

Sapphire is the second foundation stone of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:19) and the stone Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the seventy elders of Israel saw beneath the feet of the God of Israel on Sinai: "and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness" (Exod 24:10). The deep blue color speaks of heaven itself — and the Holy Spirit chose this stone as the visible boundary between God and man at the giving of the Law, and again as the second course of the eternal city's foundation. The sapphire also appears on the high priest's breastplate as the fifth stone (Exod 28:18; 39:11), and Ezekiel's vision of the throne shows it set in sapphire (Ezek 1:26; 10:1). The theological line runs: at Sinai the elders SAW sapphire beneath God and ate before Him without dying — a covenant meal — but the access was strictly bounded, only Moses could approach further; the high priest carried sapphire on his breast as he interceded once a year in the Holy of Holies; Ezekiel SAW sapphire shaped as a throne when he was carried in vision to the heavenly court; and in the New Jerusalem sapphire becomes a foundation we walk on — no longer the ceiling under which we crouch, but the floor on which the redeemed city stands. The progression is from sapphire-as-distance (Sinai) to sapphire-as-mediator (breastplate) to sapphire-as-throne (Ezekiel) to sapphire-as-foundation (New Jerusalem). The God whose glory once kept Israel at the foot of the mountain has prepared a city whose foundations rest on the very stone that once marked the unapproachable.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A precious blue stone, second foundation of the New Jerusalem and pavement beneath the feet of the God of Israel at Sinai.

expand to see more

SAPPHIRE, noun. A precious stone of a fine blue color, next in hardness to the diamond. Biblical sapphire is likely lapis lazuli (deep blue, opaque, gold-flecked) or possibly true corundum sapphire.

In Scripture, the second foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:19); the stone seen under the feet of the God of Israel by the elders at Sinai (Exod 24:10); the fifth stone of the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:18); the appearance of the throne in Ezekiel's vision (Ezek 1:26).

📖 Key Scripture

Revelation 21:19 — "And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire."

Exodus 24:10 — "And they saw the God of Israel: and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness."

Ezekiel 1:26 — "And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone: and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it."

Exodus 28:18 — "And the second row shall be an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Sapphire is corrupted when its Sinai-grounded covenant context is forgotten and the stone is treated as a generic luxury good, or when modern engagement-ring marketing replaces its theological weight with mere status signaling.

expand to see more

Reduced to commodity. The stone that paved the floor of heaven under the feet of the God of Israel — the stone that defined the visible boundary between sinful man and holy God at Sinai — is now mostly a luxury good in jewelry-store cases, priced by carat and color saturation. The biblical weight of sapphire as a witness to the unapproachable glory of God is almost entirely lost in the modern consumer association.

On the other side, the modernist commentary tradition dismisses the Exodus 24:10 vision as primitive theophany imagery — as if Israel's elders just imagined what was overhead — rather than treating the text as actual revelation that the God of glory permitted seventy-four covenant representatives to SEE the floor of heaven and to eat and drink in His presence. The text is far more startling than either treatment allows: real men, real God, real meal, real sapphire under His feet. Strip either side of this — the historicity or the typological weight — and the New Jerusalem's sapphire foundation loses its echo.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek sappheiros (G4552), Hebrew sappir (H5601) — a deep blue precious stone, likely lapis lazuli in OT contexts.

Greek sappheiros (G4552) — sapphire; second foundation stone of New Jerusalem (Rev 21:19)

Hebrew sappir (H5601) — sapphire; under God's feet at Sinai (Exod 24:10), throne in Ezekiel's vision (Ezek 1:26)

Likely identification: lapis lazuli (deep blue, opaque, with golden pyrite flecks) — the cobalt-blue "stone of heaven" of the ancient Near East

Second of the twelve stones; counterpart to jasper above it and chalcedony below it in the New Jerusalem foundation

Usage

"Under the God of Sinai was paved sapphire; over our redeemed city, sapphire becomes the second stone we stand upon."

"Ezekiel saw sapphire shaped into a throne; John saw sapphire shaped into a foundation — the same stone, the same God, the same line of glory."

"Sapphire is not a status symbol; it is the color of the floor of heaven."
